newsitem.title: USA: Universal Stainless sees reroll weakness.
newsitem.headline: Universal Stainless sees reroll weakness.

text.p: Universal Stainless & Alloy Products Inc said on Monday that import-driven price softness in reroller products was continuing and would weigh on year-end operating results.

"As we enter the fourth quarter, we are experiencing growth in several of our markets, including the reroller and power generation sectors. However, a soft pricing environment within our reroll market will continue to impact our operating results," Chief Executive Mac McAninch said in the specilaty steel maker's third-quarter earnings report.
McAninch said the company's capital-spending projects should be completed by year-end and should add to results during the first quarter of 1997.

The company said its operating margins in the third quarter improved to 15.1 percent from 10.4 percent in the second quarter, mainly because of higher volumes and lower selling, general and administrative spending.
Third-quarter gross margins benefited from continued improvement in yields, product mix and volume, the company said.
Increased profit levels in the quarter were partially offset by pricing pressure on reroll products due to increased competition from imports of bar, rod and wire, Universal said.
